title: Real-Time Observation of Lithium-ion Storage in Conversion-Type Electrode Materials after Initial Cycle
content: Conversion-type electrode materials (MX, where M is typically a transition metal and X represents oxygen, sulfur, fluorine, etc.) have garnered significant attention due to their significantly higher capacities compared to intercalation-type materials [1]. During lithiation, MX undergoes a conversion reaction, decomposing into M nanocrystals embedded within a Li-X matrix. Upon delithiation, these composites reorganize into MX nanocrystals. This initial lithium insertion and extraction cycle induces structural changes—such as, strain, defects, and microscopic rearrangement—through volume expansion [2] and fragmentation of the bulk active material. Consequently, subsequent electrochemical reactions and phase transformations may deviate from those observed in the first cycle.
